sources.title: The U.S.-China Trade Negotiation: A Contract Theory Perspective
sources.author: Angela Huyue Zhang
sources.publication_date_precision: Year on the journal pages; the official URL has a November 2020 directory. No exact publication day established.
sources.source_type: Scholarly legal article applying contract theory to published evidence, legal materials and one identified author interview
sources.read_scope: All 58 physical PDF pages, printed 809–866: abstract, contents, body, acknowledgments and notes 1–376. Sequential text reading completed through the final note; selected crucial pages also rendered and visually checked. This does not imply full reading of the article's cited works.

visual_checks.scope: Acknowledgment of January 2020 Phase One and strong prediction of instability
Trade-secret burden shifting and author interview note 81
Xi recast and draft claims; source chain in notes 104–109
Strong claim about credibility and value of punishment mechanism
Prospective agreement framing and claim that termination is the only recourse

locators.original_interview: Printed 824, note 81: author interview with an unnamed senior Chinese judge, April 2019, about trade-secret burdens of proof

source_dependence: Xi's alleged recast instruction is attributed to Buckley and Bradsher's New York Times report, note 105; no new negotiating-room interview or Chinese instruction is supplied.
The 150-page draft/deletions account in note 106 also cites Reuters 8 May 2019, already registered and independently read as TUS08; the two citations are not independent confirmations.
The agreement-in-principle claim in note 16 depends on SCMP quoting Craig Allen in June 2019.
The 1990s account draws substantially on Mertha, Mertha and Pahre, Ryan and Zeng; their underlying materials are not newly read merely by reading Zhang.
Original author interview in note 81 concerns legal design; no identity or transcript is supplied, and it does not establish negotiating authority or the cause of the May breakdown.
limitations: Much of the analysis retains prospective 2019 framing despite acknowledging January 2020 signature; it is not a detailed reading of signed Phase One or a performance study through 2026.
Categorical claims about ineffective enforcement, tariff credibility and integration's stabilizing effect are analytical propositions requiring separate tests.
The statement on printed 860 that termination is the only recourse must not describe the signed agreement, which contains the conditional suspension/remedial-action route in Article 7.4.4(b).
No authenticated May redline, Chinese reservation list or leadership clearance record is supplied.
This pass traced citations but did not newly obtain and read every NYT, SCMP or WSJ source in the May narrative.
The article's 1991 MOU label on printed 858 conflicts with its own 1992 chronology; its title of premier for Wu Yi is erroneous and must not be inherited.
sources.evidentiary_use: A mechanism for separating observable legal promises from difficult-to-verify administrative implementation, and for examining enforcement costs and political costs of wording. Useful as a rival explanation to unqualified national-style claims, not as independent proof of private Chinese decisions.

existing_sources_consulted_without_creat.scope: Prior full independent reading of Reuters 8 May 2019 report used to identify dependence and access limits.
Articles 1.3–1.5 reread in this pass; Articles 1.34–1.35, 6.2, Annex 6.1 summary, 7.4 and 8.3 independently checked in the accompanying Chapter 5 source review.
Selected bilingual clauses as specified in the Chapter 5 source review, not a new full Chinese agreement reading.
Entire January 2020 notice already independently read and visually checked in this pass; prescribed reduction of a specified tariff rate distinguished from abandonment of tariffs.

storage: Complete article PDF, extraction, retrieval manifest and selected rendered pages preserved outside Git. Only original analysis and source metadata added to the repository; shared literature ledger unchanged.
